grammar.title: 先……再…… (first… then…)
grammar.pattern: Subject + 先 + Verb Phrase 1 + 再 + Verb Phrase 2
grammar.explanation: Use 先……再…… to put two actions in order: do the first thing first, then do the second. 先 goes before the first verb, 再 before the second verb. Both parts usually share the same subject.

examples.hanzi: 我先打掃房間，再複習中文。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiān dǎsǎo fángjiān, zài fùxí Zhōngwén.
examples.gloss: I'll clean my room first, then review Chinese.

examples.hanzi: 她先洗葡萄，再拿給孩子吃。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiān xǐ pútáo, zài ná gěi háizi chī.
examples.gloss: She washes the grapes first, then gives them to the kids to eat.

examples.hanzi: 下雨了，你先帶傘，再出門。
examples.pinyin: Xià yǔ le, nǐ xiān dài sǎn, zài chū mén.
examples.gloss: It's raining; take an umbrella first, then head out.

grammar.title: 數量詞:數字 + 量詞 + 名詞
grammar.pattern: 數字 + 量詞(杯/碗/盤/本)+ 名詞
grammar.explanation: 在中文裡,說東西的數量時,數字後面一定要加量詞,才能接名詞。喝的東西用「杯」,湯麵、飯用「碗」,放在盤子上的菜用「盤」。例如:一杯果汁、兩碗麵條、三盤菜。

examples.pinyin: Wǒ diǎn le liǎng wǎn miàn tiáo.
examples.gloss: I ordered two bowls of noodles.

grammar.title: 有一點 + adjective (a bit / slightly)
grammar.explanation: 有一點 goes before an adjective to say something is 'a bit' or 'slightly' — usually about something the speaker is not happy about. In Taiwan people often shorten it to 有點. Note: you cannot say 一點有渴; 有一點 always comes first, and it is not used after the adjective.

examples.hanzi: 我有一點渴，我們去買飲料吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yìdiǎn kě, wǒmen qù mǎi yǐnliào ba.
examples.gloss: I'm a bit thirsty, let's go buy drinks.
This sentence is a bit difficult.
This camera is a bit expensive.
